pages.text: Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3d13906c5d6c81a194cdc098c32fff41 as of 2026-09-23T21:32:16.764Z: {"title":"📚 SQL Learning Path"} null ## المسار الأساسي الترتيب مبني على learning dependencies. كل موديول هنا صفحة مباشرة. مفيش صفحة فاضية في النص. ### Phase 1 — SQL Core 00 — Learning Map & Decision Framework 01 — SQL Foundations — Complete Reference 02 — Database, Schema & Data Modeling — Complete Reference 03 — Data Types, Casting & NULL Logic — Complete Reference 04 — Filtering & Conditional Logic — Complete Reference 05 — JOINs & Relationship Reasoning — Complete Reference 06 — Aggregation & Grouping — Complete Reference 07 — Subqueries & CTEs — Complete Reference 08 — Set Operations — Complete Reference 09 — Window Functions — Complete Reference 10 — Date & Time Analytics — Complete Reference 11 — Text, String & Pattern Matching — Complete Reference ### Phase 2 — Analytical & Trust Layer 12 — Analytical SQL Patterns — Comprehensive Reference 13 — Data Quality & Validation — Complete Reference ### Phase 3 — Engineering 14 — DDL, DML & Transactions — Complete Reference 15 — Database Design — Complete Reference 16 — SQL Performance Engineering — Complete Reference 17 — SQL for DWH / BI — Complete Reference ## Why this order? Understand queries → understand data → manipulate relationships → aggregate → compose advanced logic → analyze sequences/time/text → build analytical patterns → validate trust → change/design data → optimize execution → apply SQL to DWH/BI. > Important: The engineering sequence is deliberately 14 → 15 → 16 → 17: change data → design data → optimize queries → apply to DWH/BI.

pages.title: 🏁 🧭 SQL Master Decision Framework
pages.text: Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3ce3906c5d6c81028e75e4f561ff8245 as of 2026-09-23T21:47:22.120Z: {"title":"🧭 SQL Master Decision Framework"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🏁"} ## خريطة بصرية ```mermaid flowchart TD Raw["Raw data"] --> G["Structure and grain"] --> EDA["EDA, including the distribution"] --> DQ["Data quality"] --> Clean["Clean or transform"] --> An["Analysis"] --> V["Validation"] --> I["Insight"] ``` المثال 10، 10، 10، 10، 110: المتوسط 30، ومفيش ملاحظة بتساوي 30. الوسيط 10. > ختام مكتبة Intermediate SQL: عقلية المحلل، ودليل قرار شامل يلخص كل تقنيات السلسلة في مكان واحد. # 1. EDA مش وقت ضايع أبدًا قبل أي تحليل معقد، افهم البيانات بعمق. سير العمل المُوصى به: ```txt Raw Data ↓ Understand structure & grain ↓ EDA ↓ Data Quality checks ↓ Cleaning / Transformation ↓ Analysis ↓ Validation ↓ Insight / Decision ``` # 2. الإحصائيات الوصفية مش كافية متفسّرش بس AVG أو الـvariance أو أي إحصائية وصفية تانية من غير ما تفحص الـdistribution. مثال: ```txt 10, 10, 10, 10, 110 ``` المتوسط 30، لكن مفيش observation فعلًا بتساوي 30. الـdistribution متأثرة جدًا بقيمة متطرفة. دايمًا اعتبر: - المتوسط (Mean) - الوسيط (Median) - التشتت (Spread) - شكل الـdistribution - الـoutliers - حجم العينة (Sample size) > قاعدة: المقياس الوصفي بيصف البيانات؛ مش بديل عن فهم البيانات. # 3. توقّع بيانات غير نظيفة دايمًا دوّر بنشاط على: - قيم مفقودة - تكرارات (Duplicates) - قيم غير صالحة - عدم اتساق في حالة الأحرف - مسافات زايدة - اختلافات في علامات الترقيم - تصنيفات غير متوقعة - فترات زمنية مفقودة - Outliers # 4. تحقق من الافتراضات متحوّلش أي حدس (intuition) لاستنتاج business من غير ما تختبره. مثال افتراض: > "مبيعات الويكند أقل." تحقق بالبيانات: ```sql SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM sale_date) AS day_of_week, COUNT(*) AS sales FROM sales GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1; ``` # 5. كن فضوليًا لما أي metric يتغيّر بشكل غير متوقع، اسأل: - أي segment اللي اتغيّر؟ - امتى حصل التغيير؟ - هل التغيير حقيقي ولا مشكلة في جودة البيانات؟ - هل تغيّر الـbusiness process؟ - هل تغيّر الـdata pipeline؟ - هل النمط ده ثابت عبر أبعاد (dimensions) مختلفة؟ الهدف مش بس إنتاج رقم؛ الهدف إنك تفهم ليه الرقم ده بالظبط. # 6. استخدم توثيق PostgreSQL مش لازم تحفظ كل دالة. لازم تعرف: 1. إيه نوع العملية اللي محتاجها. 2. أي عائلة دوال ذات صلة. 3. إزاي تتحقق من الـsyntax والـarguments وأنواع الإرجاع والـedge cases من التوثيق الرسمي. --- # 7. دليل القرار النهائي / Cheat Sheet | لو السؤال... | فكّر في... | | --- | --- | | تصنيف الصفوف لفئات business | CASE WHEN | | عد الصفوف اللي بتحقق شرط | COUNT(CASE WHEN ... THEN ... END) | | جمع القيم بشرط معين | SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN value ELSE 0 END) | | حساب نسبة مئوية من شرط | مؤشر 0/1 + AVG() | | تنظيف اختلافات حالة الأحرف | LOWER() / UPPER() | | إزالة مسافات البداية/النهاية | TRIM() / LTRIM() / RTRIM() | | البحث عن نمط (pattern) | LIKE / ILIKE | | استخراج أحرف بموضع ثابت | LEFT() / RIGHT() / SUBSTRING() | | تقسيم نص باستخدام delimiter | SPLIT_PART() | | دمج نصوص | CONCAT() / \|\| | | تحويلات مختلفة لصيغ مختلفة | CASE WHEN | | mappings صريحة كتير من فوضوي لنظيف | جدول recoding مؤقت + JOIN | | استخراج سنة/شهر/يوم من تاريخ | EXTRACT() / DATE_PART() | | تجميع timestamps في شهور/ساعات/إلخ | DATE_TRUNC() | | إنشاء تواريخ/ساعات مفقودة | GENERATE_SERIES() • LEFT JOIN | | إنشاء time buckets مخصصة | bins مولّدة + range join | | الصف/القيمة السابقة | LAG() | | الصف/القيمة التالية | LEAD() | | التغيّر مقابل الفترة السابقة | current - LAG(current) | | متوسط الفجوة بين الأحداث | LAG() ← CTE/subquery ← AVG() | | تسلسل مستقل لكل عميل/منتج/إلخ | PARTITION BY • ORDER BY | ## القواعد الذهبية للمحلل 1. استكشف قبل ما تستنتج. 2. اعرف الـgrain قبل الـaggregation. 3. افحص القيم المميزة والتكرارات للنص التصنيفي. 4. عامل NULL، الـstring الفارغ، والمسافات كمفاهيم منفصلة. 5. طبّع النص قبل الـgrouping لما يكون مناسبًا. 6. استخدم EXTRACT للمكونات، وDATE_TRUNC للـtime buckets. 7. استخدم GENERATE_SERIES لما الفترات المفقودة نفسها تكون مهمة تحليليًا. 8. استخدم LAG/LEAD للمقارنات بين صف وصف. 9. استخدم PARTITION BY لما التسلسل لازم يكون مستقل لكل كيان. 10. متعتمدش على المتوسطات من غير ما تفهم الـdistribution. 11. توقّع مشاكل جودة البيانات. 12. تحقق من افتراضاتك بالبيانات. 13. استخدم التوثيق كجزء طبيعي من سير عملك. 14. اسأل "ليه؟" لما النتيجة تكون غير متوقعة.

pages.title: 🎓 Associate Data Analyst in SQL — Master Map
pages.text: Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3d63906c5d6c81669712ce8af7ac5426 as of 2026-09-09T13:47:24.887Z: {"title":"Associate Data Analyst in SQL — Master Map"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🎓"} Purpose: Align the SQL Master Library with the current DataCamp — Associate Data Analyst in SQL track while preserving the deeper architecture already built in Notion. This page is the course-by-course audit and navigation layer. ## 📌 Current DataCamp Reference DataCamp currently lists 11 courses in the track, with two bonus projects. The track is currently shown as 39 hours, updated 05/2026, and is designed to prepare learners for the Associate Data Analyst in SQL certification. [Official Track](https://www.datacamp.com/tracks/associate-data-analyst-in-sql) ## 🧭 Audit Legend - 🟢 COVERED — the required DataCamp scope has a clear canonical owner in Notion. - 🟡 PARTIAL / DISTRIBUTED — covered, but DataCamp combines material that Notion intentionally splits across multiple canonical notes. - 🔵 EXTENDED — Notion goes substantially deeper than DataCamp; keep the deeper material. - 🟠 GAP — a DataCamp topic is not yet clearly represented as a canonical note. - 🟥 DUPLICATE RISK — topic exists in multiple places and needs ownership/linking rather than another rewrite. --- # 01 — Introduction to SQL DataCamp scope: relational databases, tables/rows/columns, data types, basic querying, SELECT, DISTINCT, aliases, views/basic query concepts. Coverage: 🟢 COVERED + EXTENDED Canonical Notion sources Audit finding: DataCamp introduces the concepts; Notion goes further into grain, logical query processing order, NULL/three-valued logic, determinism, keys, and correctness. Do not split these foundations into extra copies. KEEP AS-IS --- # 02 — Intermediate SQL DataCamp scope: filtering, comparison, aggregation, grouping, sorting, HAVING, aliases, rounding, query readability/style. Coverage: 🟢 COVERED + EXTENDED Canonical Notion sources Ownership: WHERE, predicates, HAVING, and CASE → 04. Aggregation, grouping, conditional aggregation, KPI-safe aggregation → 06. Audit finding: The split is intentional and better than mirroring DataCamp's chapter boundaries literally. KEEP AS-IS --- # ⭐ Bonus Project — Analyzing Students' Mental Health DataCamp role: early applied project using data manipulation / exploration on student mental-health data. Coverage: 🟡 PARTIAL / DISTRIBUTED Notion sources Audit finding: no clearly matching standalone project note was identified. Do not duplicate the project yet. Add a project index only if you want a dedicated portfolio/project layer later. --- # 03 — Joining Data in SQL DataCamp scope: vertical combination (UNION), horizontal joins, multiple-column joins, outer joins, cross joins, self joins, set theory, nested queries, semi/anti joins. Coverage: 🟢 COVERED + EXTENDED Canonical Notion sources Audit finding: Notion is materially deeper on cardinality, fan-out, row multiplication, composite join keys, safe pre-aggregation, JOIN vs EXISTS, and join validation. EXTENDED — preserve depth. citeturn897402search0 --- # 04 — Data Manipulation in SQL DataCamp scope: CASE, subqueries, correlated queries, CTEs, window functions, analytical query composition. Coverage: 🟢 COVERED + EXTENDED Canonical Notion sources Audit finding: Notion already follows the right canonical-ownership model: CASE → 04, Subqueries/CTEs → 07, Window Functions → 09; 12 is applied/case-study material rather than theory. citeturn897402search2 --- # 05 — PostgreSQL Summary Stats and Window Functions DataCamp scope: window syntax, OVER, ORDER BY, PARTITION BY, ROW_NUMBER, fetching, ranking, paging, aggregate windows, frames, moving/running calculations, pivoting, ROLLUP, CUBE. Coverage: 🟢 COVERED + EXTENDED Canonical Notion sources Deep subnotes Audit finding: This is one of the strongest matches in the library. The 09 master + subnotes maps directly to DataCamp's four chapters. DataCamp explicitly covers ROWS vs RANGE, ranking/fetching/paging, and ROLLUP/CUBE. citeturn324219search1 --- # 06 — Functions for Manipulating Data in PostgreSQL DataCamp scope: PostgreSQL data types, arrays, date/time functions, text functions, full-text search, extensions, fuzzy matching. Coverage: 🟢 COVERED + EXTENDED Canonical Notion source Key subnotes Audit finding: DataCamp's course is almost a direct match to your PostgreSQL specialization architecture. Your PostgreSQL hub explicitly enforces the correct boundary: core SQL concept in Core; PostgreSQL-specific behavior/syntax in the PostgreSQL layer. citeturn324219search0 --- # 07 — Introduction to Statistics DataCamp scope: summary statistics, probability, distributions, sampling/CLT, correlation, hypothesis testing, statistical significance, data types and interpretation. Coverage: 🟢 COVERED + EXTENDED Canonical Notion source Applied supplements Audit finding: The statistics reference is deeper than the track-level description and includes population/sample, descriptive and inferential statistics, probability, distributions, CLT, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, A/B testing, correlation, confounding, and Type I/II errors. DataCamp's current course explicitly covers center/spread, probability, distributions, correlation, and hypothesis testing. citeturn324219search3 --- # 08 — Exploratory Data Analysis in SQL DataCamp scope: database discovery, relationships/foreign keys, missingness, data types, numeric exploration, categorical/text exploration, date/time exploration, anomalies, cleaning, temporary tables. Coverage: 🟡 PARTIAL / DISTRIBUTED — intentional Canonical Notion sources Audit finding: DataCamp deliberately packages EDA into one course; your library intentionally decomposes it by responsibility. The EDA skill is fully represented, but the navigation is missing one course-level index that says “these five canonical notes together = DataCamp EDA.” ACTION: add an EDA aggregation/index page, not duplicate content. DataCamp's current course explicitly includes table/relationship discovery, missing values, numeric summaries, categorical/unstructured text, dates, and temporary tables. citeturn324219search2 --- # 09 — Data-Driven Decision Making in SQL DataCamp scope: business intelligence with MovieNow, simple SQL decision making, customer preferences/engagement, advanced SQL decision analysis, OLAP with CUBE, ROLLUP, GROUPING SETS. Coverage: 🟢 COVERED + EXTENDED Canonical Notion source Supporting references Audit finding: 12 is already explicitly designed as the applied MovieNow layer, while theory stays in the canonical modules. This is exactly the right separation. DataCamp's current course is also based on MovieNow and includes OLAP operators. citeturn268355search0 --- # 10 — Understanding Data Visualization DataCamp scope: visualizing distributions; histograms/box plots; two-variable analysis; scatter/line/bar/dot/pie/rose plots; scales; dual axes; sensory overload; chartjunk; interpretation. Coverage: 🟢 COVERED + EXTENDED Canonical Notion source Supporting references Audit finding: your visualization library is broader than DataCamp because it adds dashboard design, accessibility, Power BI implementation, ethics/integrity, interview prep, and storytelling integration. DataCamp's current course centers on distributions and two-variable visualization plus common pitfalls. citeturn268355search1 --- # 11 — Data Communication Concepts DataCamp scope: storytelling, translating technical results, audience/personas, selecting data/statistics/visuals, written reports, oral presentations, delivery pitfalls. Coverage: 🟢 COVERED + EXTENDED Canonical Notion sources Audit finding: the Notion storytelling library maps well to DataCamp's storytelling → audience → written → oral progression, and is considerably deeper. DataCamp's current course explicitly covers storytelling, audience-appropriate translation, data/statistics/visual choice, reports, and oral presentations. citeturn268355search2 --- # 🧪 Cross-Track Gaps & Structural Findings ## 1. No major knowledge gap found The core DataCamp track is strongly represented in the current Notion library. Most “gaps” are actually navigation gaps caused by Notion being more granular than DataCamp. ## 2. Biggest structural mismatch: EDA DataCamp packages EDA as one course, while Notion distributes it across Database Exploration + Data Quality + Numeric EDA/Statistics + Date/Time + Text. This is good architecture, but it needs a single course-level index. ## 3. Biggest duplicate risk: Core SQL vs PostgreSQL You already have the correct boundary rule: core SQL explains the general concept; PostgreSQL explains PostgreSQL-specific behavior. Preserve that rule and link rather than copy. fileciteturn28file0 ## 4. Biggest strength: Analytical correctness Your notes are deeper than DataCamp on grain, cardinality, fan-out, row multiplication, KPI definitions, NULL semantics, validation, reconciliation, and DWH/BI implications. fileciteturn14file0 fileciteturn15file0 fileciteturn17file0 ## 5. What should NOT be moved into the DataCamp structure Keep these as separate layers rather than forcing them into the 11-course sequence: - SQL Performance Engineering - DDL / DML / Transactions - Database Design - SQL for DWH / BI - SQL Interview - Practical SQL Toolkit - PostgreSQL Specialization These are adjacent/extended capabilities, not missing DataCamp chapters. The existing Master Library already separates them intentionally. fileciteturn7file0 --- # ✅ Final Audit Result | DataCamp item | Coverage | Canonical handling | Action | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Introduction to SQL | 🟢 | 01–03 | Keep | | Intermediate SQL | 🟢 | 04 + 06 + Foundations | Keep | | Student Mental Health Project | 🟡 | Applied across 04/06/13 | Don't duplicate | | Joining Data in SQL | 🟢🔵 | 05 + 08 + 07 | Keep + preserve depth | | Data Manipulation in SQL | 🟢 | 04 + 07 + 09 + 12 | Keep | | PostgreSQL Window Functions | 🟢 | 09 + subnotes | Keep | | PostgreSQL Data Functions | 🟢 | 18 + subnotes | Keep | | Introduction to Statistics | 🟢🔵 | Statistics Reference | Keep | | Exploratory Data Analysis in SQL | 🟡 | 02 + 10 + 11 + 13 + Numeric EDA | Add index only | | Data-Driven Decision Making in SQL | 🟢 | 12 + Decision Framework | Keep | | Understanding Data Visualization | 🟢🔵 | Visualization Hub | Keep | | Data Communication Concepts | 🟢🔵 | Storytelling Hub | Keep | | Motorcycle Part Sales Project | 🟡 | Applied/project layer | Add project index later | ## 🎯 Recommended Final Architecture A. DataCamp Track View 11 Courses + 2 Projects → this page B. Core Learning View 00 → 01 → 02 → 03 → 04 → 05 → 06 → 07 → 08 → 09 → 10 → 11 → 12 → 13 → 14 → 15 → 16 → 17 C. Specialist Views PostgreSQL · Interview · Practical Toolkit · DWH/BI · Performance D. Applied View Projects / Case Studies / Business Analysis > Bottom line: Do not rebuild the library to imitate DataCamp one-to-one. Keep the current canonical knowledge architecture and use the DataCamp Master Map as a second navigation lens. The only real structural addition identified in this audit is an EDA course-level index and, optionally later, a small Projects index. 08 — Exploratory Data Analysis in SQL — Notion Course Index ⭐ DataCamp SQL Track — Projects Index
